title: Forces and Motion
seo_title: Grade 8 Forces and Motion Worksheets: Net Force, Inertia and Newton's Second Law
standard_text: Plan an investigation to provide evidence that the change in an object's motion depends on the sum of the forces on the object and the mass of the object.
meta_desc: Free middle school science worksheets on forces and motion (NGSS MS-PS2-2): net force diagrams, balanced and unbalanced forces, inertia, and how force and mass affect acceleration. 100 practice questions with answers.
key_big: Motion changes when the net force is not zero.
key_sub: A bigger net force causes a bigger change in motion; a bigger mass causes a smaller change (a = F ÷ m).
body_html:
How to think about it

The net force is the total of all forces on an object. Add forces in the same direction; subtract forces in opposite directions.

25 N right − 10 N left = 15 N to the right. Unbalanced forces change motion in the direction of the net force.

Newton's first law: with no net force, an object stays at rest or keeps moving at the same speed in a straight line (inertia). Newton's second law: the change in motion (acceleration) depends on net force and mass, a = F ÷ m. More force → more change; more mass → less change.

Example

Forces of 30 N right and 30 N left act on a box at rest. What happens?

Net force = 0.

Answer: It stays at rest.

Example

The same 20 N pushes a 2 kg cart and a 4 kg cart. Which accelerates more?

a = F ÷ m

20 ÷ 2 = 10; 20 ÷ 4 = 5

Answer: the 2 kg cart

Common mistakes

  • Thinking a moving object needs a net force to keep moving.
  • Adding forces that point in opposite directions.
  • Thinking more mass speeds up more with the same push.

faq.q: How do you find net force?
faq.a: Add forces that point in the same direction and subtract forces that point in opposite directions.

faq.q: What happens when the forces on an object are balanced?
faq.a: The object keeps doing what it was doing: it stays at rest or keeps moving at a steady speed in a straight line.

faq.q: How do force and mass affect motion?
faq.a: A larger net force causes a larger acceleration. A larger mass causes a smaller acceleration for the same force.

items.q: What does Newton's first law say?
c: For every action there is a reaction.
Moving objects always slow down by themselves.
An object keeps doing what it is doing unless an unbalanced force acts on it.
items.e: This is inertia.

items.q: A hockey puck slides on ice and slowly stops. Why?

items.e: Without friction, it would keep sliding.

items.q: What does Newton's second law say?

Mass has no effect on motion.
items.e: More force, more acceleration; more mass, less acceleration.
